Run summary

How to read this: the tables of the run's comparison.md, one column per leg; the same numbers appear in the charts below. Marks are explained in the glossary.

1Is this run valid?

Before looking at speeds: every leg must have loaded the whole corpus, with no errors and with its containers alive.

How to read this: ✓ok met · !warning use with care · ✗fail those numbers are not comparable · – not applicable.

2Results

Headline numbers by leg

How to read this: pick a leg; every leg gets the same tiles. The comparison with the previous run appears only for legs that have data in that run.

Throughput by suite, all legs

How to read this: longer bar = more per second (the search indexing panel is in seconds: shorter is better); each panel has its own scale, so compare legs within a panel, not across panels.

† ‡ ⚠ validity marks (see glossary)

Latency by suite (logarithmic scale)

How to read this: the dot is the median (p50), the vertical tick is the p95 and the end of the line is the p99; further left is faster and each axis mark is 10 times the previous one.

3Detail

Timeline and host load

How to read this: pick All to compare every leg at once: one line per leg in its own colour (dashed line and diamond markers = the leg with Elasticsearch), with the leg name at the end of the line and the phases of each leg in a lane below. Pick a single leg to see its phase bands. The line is the Docker host load (1-minute average);

There is only one reading at the start and one at the end of each phase; between readings the line is an interpolation. Each band covers the whole suite step (k6 plus diagnostic captures), not just the load. In the All view the legs are aligned at their own start, not at the same clock time.

Bulk Import (/ui/bulk-import, $bulk-submit) by phase

How to read this: each bar is the time until the data can be searched; shorter is better. The official clock adds ingest and search indexing; the NDJSON conversion beforehand is shown separately. Where indexing runs inline (during ingest), as on the Elasticsearch legs, it has no bar of its own: its time is inside the ingest bar. The colour of each bar is the leg.

conversion (not in the total)ingestsearch indexing (deferred rebuild)

Batch/Transaction Import (/ui/batch, k6 import) by phase

How to read this: each bar is the whole k6 step; shorter is better. The solid part is the import scenario, which is what resources/s divides by; the light part is k6 setup(), which seeds the Bundles before the load starts. Below each bar: resources, resources/s, Bundles completed out of the target († if the corpus is incomplete) and the error rate (‡ above the threshold).

k6 setup() (seed Bundles)import scenario

Latency per Bundle (logarithmic scale)

How to read this: time of one whole Bundle (iteration_duration): the dot is p50, the vertical tick p95 and the end of the line p99; further left is faster.

Import: Batch/Transaction vs Bulk (resources/s)

How to read this: for each leg, the solid bar is the Batch/Transaction Import and the outlined bar is the Bulk Import; longer is faster.

Batch/Transaction (/ui/batch)Bulk (/ui/bulk-import)

These are different workloads: the Batch/Transaction Import is concurrent k6 clients posting Bundles, and the Bulk Import is a single $bulk-submit job; compare them as two ways to load data, not as the same test.

SQL-on-FHIR $sql-run by view (logarithmic scale)

How to read this: one panel per ViewDefinition run by the sql-run suite; the dot is p50, the tick p95 and the end of the line p99 of the requests to that view; further left is faster.

Search by query shape

How to read this: the search average hides slow queries; here each row is a query type, the dark part reaches the median and the light part reaches the p95.

Percentiles by index without interpolation, same as search_by_shape.py in CI; that is why they do not match k6 exactly.

How to read this: one point per run (leg colour = this run, orange = other runs), higher is better; with a single data point per date and different hosts, the line shows context, not a proven trend.

Glossary

LegA storage combination tested separately (e.g. postgres + Elasticsearch).
VU (virtual user)A simulated client with a single request in flight; N VUs are N clients at once, not N req/s.
req/sHTTP requests completed per second (more is better).
resources/sFHIR resources stored per second; used for Batch/Transaction Import and Bulk Import, where one request carries many resources.
p50 / p95 / p99Response time that 50 %, 95 % or 99 % of requests do not exceed (less is better).
Err%Percentage of requests with an HTTP error; it does not check whether the content is correct.
Checks ✓/✗k6 script verifications that passed or failed (e.g. "the Bundle was imported").
Load (load average)Average number of processes wanting CPU; above the CPU count there is waiting.
